profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI, also known as Ai2, is a nonprofit AI research organization founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. Led by Ali Farhadi, the organization describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering on key problems in artificial intelligence, guided by open, collaborative, and inclusive principles aimed at producing safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems. Its work spans foundational AI research as well as applied areas including climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife protection.

Ai2 maintains notable partnerships with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the NSF on the Open Multimodal AI Infrastructure to Accelerate Science project, and Google Cloud, which the organization says supports development of its open AI models and scientific research platforms. Two tracked products reflect its research-focused, openly available approach: OLMo, an open-source language model developed with fully open training data and an emphasis on research transparency, and Semantic Scholar, an AI-powered academic search tool offering paper summaries and citation graphs.

The site holds no record of litigation or MCP server presence associated with Ai2.
